cells.tense: What you are is showing, and your hands are steady on the pen while it shows.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Look again at the last few times something got your whole attention. Trace the shape running through them. What did those moments share that you didn't have to work out?
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves your attention before you could argue the case for it. Most people build the case first and only then find out it was the wrong thing to spend a year on. You know on the way in.

It is a quiet thing to watch, and nothing about it needs defending. The practice is to look for the shape underneath. Look again at the last few times something got your whole attention and trace the shape running through them — what they shared, what you saw before you could explain it. Write a line about it and leave everything else alone. Naming the shape is what lets you choose it next time instead of only following where it pulls. The showing can stay unannounced; the aim is only that you can see your own hand in it.
cells.sheetLine: You know what deserves you before you can argue it.
cells.place: where you know which things deserve your attention

cells.tense: You will be reaching for the answer before the thing has had its moment.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Take one subject you've already settled in your mind and study it as though you'd just met it: what's actually here today, before your verdict.
cells.core:
You recognize what deserves attention, and lately the recognition runs faster than the thing being recognized. You will be reaching for the answer before the moment has had its chance. What should be slow goes quick; a person, a practice, a place gets filed the instant it arrives, and the morning that could have surprised you is already sorted.

Nothing is wrong with what you've made. The repair is smaller than the problem. Take one subject you've already settled and study it as though you'd just met it — what's actually here today, before your verdict — and decide nothing from it. Ten minutes unlabelled won't cost you the thing itself. It puts the door back where you can walk through it, instead of arriving already on the far side.
cells.sheetLine: Your answer arrives before the thing has a chance to.

cells.tense: What you came to be has been finished, and you have been standing behind it, letting the room fill.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Pick out one subject you know counts, from everything wanting you, and give it your attention today — this one, not the others — and hold to it.
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves attention; where this lands, it stays inside you. There is a version of restraint that looks like humbleness and works like a held breath — the person with the read on the room, waiting to be consulted, keeping the light low enough that nobody has to react. The people near you have mostly worked it out for themselves.

Insight won't restore it; a direction will. Pick out one subject you know counts, from everything wanting you, and give it your attention today — this one, not the others — and hold to it. One thing, chosen and then simply done. You don't need an audience or a speech. The first move is the hard part; the direction does the rest.
cells.sheetLine: You know what counts and you keep it to yourself.

cells.tense: Something is arriving in you all the time and you have no account of it.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: At the next moment that matters to you, pause half a beat before you respond, and catch what lands before the reply assembles itself.
cells.core:
People bring you things because you can see which part counts. They ask what matters and you give them the straight answer, sometimes before the question has finished, and then you carry on with your day. It rarely registers as something you did.

So let the next real moment be new. When something that matters lands, pause half a beat before you respond, and catch what arrives before the reply assembles itself. That first knowing is yours; the difference between what came to you and what the conversation required is the whole thing. No one needs to hear about it. Catch one arriving, and the follow-up becomes easier to notice — including on the days it has stopped.
cells.sheetLine: You hand over the true answer and call it nothing.

attempts.check: The record says 'radiance without ego' but nothing in it establishes that others are blinded; 'blinding others' is the record's own telescoped image, so I render Too Much as a lean toward being seen rather than a claim about harm done. A reader could reasonably say the person is just private or modest, not dimmed, so Too Little locates the standing-back and says nothing about when or why it started. The ask survives a wrong read: skipping a habit, listing what lives on another's say-so, picking one thing, or waiting to be asked all teach the person something about where their knowing sits, whether or not my read fits. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you've been standing behind your own knowing' — cut, because the record doesn't support that they know it's there.

Too Little still runs the risk of certifying that the person knows the good thing — the record's own seat says the capacity is there and the status says it is dimmed, not absent, so locating the standing-back is licit but I no longer claim what they will choose. The asks survive a wrong read: each teaches where attention actually goes, whether or not my read fits. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line asserting they have been hiding their light on purpose — cut; the dimming is not a decision I can see from here.
